headline: Volvo EX60 launches Bühler megacasting; EU carbon and scrap rules tighten

summary.text: Volvo is bringing Bühler megacasting to the road in the EX60, a concrete sign that OEMs are insourcing large structures that could pull volume from Lindner's shock towers and longitudinal members.

European Aluminium welcomes the EU ETS changes and proposes a 1.7% LRF and a 2040 extension of indirect cost compensation, which will shape carbon and energy costs for aluminium and for Lindner's casting operations.
European aluminium scrap curbs could raise costs and tighten secondary alloy supply, which Lindner needs for low-carbon structural castings.
Competitor TRIMET has opened a German aluminium recycling plant, which strengthens its CO2 position. It may also offer Lindner a source of low-carbon secondary alloy.
Rio Tinto and RevoCast are expanding low-carbon aluminium billet supply, a possible lower-CO2 source for meeting EU OEM carbon targets.

actions.text: Sales lead: assess which Volvo parts are exposed to the EX60 megacasting shift and prepare a mid-size integrated casting or ramp-up know-how pitch for Volvo and similar OEMs.
Purchasing: request low-carbon and secondary alloy quotes from TRIMET, Rio Tinto and RevoCast, and check how scrap curbs would affect current supply contracts.
Finance and energy lead: model the impact of the proposed ETS changes and 2040 indirect cost compensation extension on energy and aluminium costs, and brief the managing director.
